source.title: Comparing Sparsified MLPs and Transcoders: Many Transcoder Features Are Neurons in Disguise

page_placements.theme: Native neurons match or beat dictionary features on some tests, and much dictionary activity duplicates single MLP neurons

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper directly compares neuron-based attribution graphs with transcoder-based graphs using replacement score, a different measure from the claim’s preliminary audit.
record.gate_note: The paper does not audit the positive and negative poles of neurons for named jobs or test explanations against held-out activating examples as the claim versions specify. Its measured transcoder-feature alignment with neurons is relevant to the subject but is not a measurement of the share of neuron poles with one or two jobs; those results are recorded with versions ["none"]. The replacement-score comparison in Figure 15 is recorded for V5. Cited results from other work and the deliberately induced distress behavior are not recorded as results bearing on these versions.
record.test_reason: The study builds attribution graphs directly from sparsified MLP neurons in Gemma 3 4B and compares their Replacement Score with transcoder graphs (Figure 15). This is a different method aimed at V5's question of whether neurons suffice as circuit units. Its main transcoder-feature alignment results (Table 4) measure a related but different construct. They are not shares of neuron poles with one or two jobs, so they bear on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors' central claim is that many transcoder features are 'neurons in disguise'. These neuron features carry most of transcoders' Jacobian faithfulness and cross-seed stability, while non-neuron features are unstable and stay near initialization. So top-k thresholded, sign-split neurons are a stronger interpretability and circuit basis than assumed. They add that neuron attribution graphs have lower replacement scores than Gemmascope graphs but are useful. Transcoders win on reconstruction (FVU) and fine-grained concepts such as bigrams, and neurons are polysemantic across broad activation ranges.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares neuron-based attribution graphs and sparsified MLPs with transcoder-based graphs; it does not reproduce the Qwen3-32B pole audit or explanation-testing procedure in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Neuron-feature prevalence varies with model, layer, transcoder architecture and alignment threshold; the paper notes thresholds from 0.6 to 0.9 and greater prevalence in later layers. The neuron-attribution replacement-score comparison is shown over L0.

fits_no_version.finding: Sort evals (Claude Haiku judge, Gemma 3 4B L22): neurons' top activations score comparably to Gemmascope features. Under quantile sampling across the activation range, neuron scores degrade noticeably relative to transcoder features (Fig 3b, Section 2.5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neurons look monosemantic at their top activations but are polysemantic across their broader activation range, more so than transcoder features.

fits_no_version.finding: Transcoder features aligned to single neurons are a small share of dictionaries (4.5%–39.4% at 66% depth) but supply 38%–83% of feature activations in late layers, rising with Gemma model size (Table 4). An MoE transcoder shows 15.8% (baseline) vs 30.7% (neuron init).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Much of what transcoders learn in late layers duplicates individual MLP neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: Neurons match or exceed transcoders on 113-task sparse probing (Table 5). They fail bigram detection: top-1 example contains the target bigram 0.0% for Gemma 3 4B neurons vs 75.6% for Gemmascope, and 20.1% for Gemma 4 MoE neurons (Table 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dense-model neurons do not represent rare fine-grained concepts such as bigrams monosemantically.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: Interpretability as a Science
record.problems: For the claim’s neuron-interpretability question, the evidence is indirect: transcoder-feature alignment is not a measure of named neuron jobs. The authors state that the work is restricted to base models, mostly English, and sparse high-magnitude single-token activations; it includes no systematic human evaluation. MoE and cross-layer analyses are preliminary. Replacement-score results for the neuron-versus-transcoder comparison are presented as curves, with no numerical uncertainty stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were omitted due to the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B pole audit and no shares of poles with one or two jobs or not yet understood.
No share-of-poles audit in any model. Transcoder-feature alignment fractions (Table 4, Appendix O MoE) do not estimate named-job shares. No trillion-parameter models.
No vision models or InceptionV1 cat-and-car analysis.
No test of how interpretable-neuron share rises with tools or architecture in vision models. The MoE bigram observation (Table 7) is preliminary and not about interpretable-neuron share.
Only Gemma 3 4B with 30 prompts for the Replacement Score comparison. No test on models of very large scale. Full explanation of behaviour is not established.
No test of whether written explanations from activating examples predict held-out firing.

missing.what: Numeric Replacement Score summaries in the Figure 15 legend (neurons 0.64, TopK 0.55, GS small 0.56, GS big 0.74).
KL/FVU of neuron-based replacement models: untrained pruned neurons have high KL and FVU>1; with a trained linear map, KL falls below transcoders while FVU stays higher; replicated across models.
Sort-eval monosemanticity of sign-split neurons vs Gemmascope under top vs quantile sampling.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's sign-split neurons resemble the claim's 'poles', but no study-wide share of poles with one or two jobs is reported. The 'red' case study finds three polysemantic layer-22 neurons, anecdotal and not a rate. The distress circuit is built on a deliberately elicited steering vector, so it is not a rate result. Comparator rows R32–R34 are transcoder baselines; their states should not read as 'observed' for the neuron claim. The legend/text inconsistency for GS L0-small should be checked against the figure.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit, neuron-pole job counts, or estimate of unexplained poles.
The paper studies models up to 27B and includes preliminary MoE work, but it does not measure the claim’s shares of neuron poles with one or two jobs, nor scaling to trillions of parameters.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car example or test of pose detection versus superposition.
No test of the claim’s InceptionV1-sized vision-model estimates or of the proposed architecture/tool explanation for those estimates.

Tests neuron-based attribution graphs against transcoder graphs using replacement score; it does not establish that neuron graphs fully explain arbitrary model behavior or test the claim’s specific reconstruction-error wording.
No test of explanations written from activating examples for predicting where the same neuron fires.
No automated neuron-explanation score based on simulated activations on new text.

rows.subject: Gemma 3 4B
rows.operation_detail: Compared replacement scores of attribution graphs built from sparsified MLP neurons with transcoder-based attribution graphs.
rows.note: Text says Gemmascope graphs, but not TopK transcoders, have higher replacement score than sparsified MLPs around the practical L0 range. The neuron graphs are nevertheless presented as useful for circuit analysis.
rows.check: Value is readable from the Figure 15 legend: Neurons (RelP, k=128) summary 0.64, not 'figure only'. Neuron graphs beat the TopK transcoder (0.55) but trail Gemmascope L0-big (0.74), and their score stays below 1 at practical L0. The legend's 0.56 for GS L0-small conflicts with the text, which says Gemmascopes beat neurons in the 10–100 L0 range. The legend number is probably a summary over L0; flag this for researchers.

source_check.notes: The Figure 15 legend values (0.64/0.55/0.56/0.74) are per-method summaries the text does not define; GS-small 0.56 equals Table 12's median RS. The prose says both Gemmascopes, not TopK, beat neurons around L0 10-100. Neuron graphs on Gemma 3 27B-it and Gemma 4 26B-A4B are qualitative only. The uncorrected pruned-neuron FVU above 1 is specific to Gemma 3 4B (App A.1).

statements.correction: Figure 15 legend (per-method summaries, no L0 range stated): Gemmascope L0-big 0.74, neurons RelP k=128 0.64, Gemmascope L0-small 0.56, TopK k=64 0.55. Sec 2.4: both Gemmascopes, not TopK, have higher RS than sparsified MLPs around L0 10-100. Caption: L0-big plus L0-small are best at low L0. Sec 2.2 (Gemma 3 4B): untrained pruned neurons give high KL and FVU above 1; with a trained linear map, KL is below the transcoders'.
statements.problem: It puts the legend summaries (0.74 vs 0.64) 'in the practical L0 range', but the text gives no numbers for that range. It also narrows the text's claim to L0-big only, then lists L0-small 0.56, which is below neurons on the legend.

statements.correction: RS comparison: Gemma 3 4B only (Fig 15). Neuron RelP graphs also on Gemma 3 27B-it (distress/apology circuit, features filtered by Claude Haiku; Fig 16, App L-M) and Gemma 4 26B-A4B (23 prompts, expert-influence Gini only; App N). Neither has RS or ablation.
statements.problem: This study's only quantitative neuron-graph test is on Gemma 3 4B. But it also builds neuron attribution graphs at 26-27B, so 'rests only on the original at those scales' misses qualitative evidence of the kind the original gives (a graph without ablation).

statements.correction: Sec 2.2: on Gemma 3 4B, untrained top-k pruned neurons have high KL and FVU above 1; a trained linear map on the pruned MLP output brings KL below the transcoders'. App A.1: 'On Gemma 3 4B the none FVU exceeds 1', likely from the post-feedforward LayerNorm; across models, transcoders have higher KL than the neuron variants.
statements.problem: It states the uncorrected pruned-neuron result for the whole study. The text reports it for Gemma 3 4B, and App A.1 says FVU above 1 is specific to Gemma 3 4B, likely from its post-feedforward LayerNorm.

statements.correction: Table 4, all transcoders: neuron-feature share of dictionary 4.5% (Qwen 3 1.7B mwhanna) to 39.4% (Llama 3.1 8B LXTC-8x); NF% acts 38.0% (Llama 3.2 1B mntss CLT) to 82.8% (Gemma 3 27B GS-small). Gemma 3 Gemmascope only: 5.9%-37.1% of dictionary, 57.5%-82.8% of activations. GS-small rises 5.9->8.9->15.6->37.1% and 57.9->63.8->73.7->82.8% from 1B to 27B.
